description: CIE XYZ (D65) to CIELAB and CIELCh, CIE 15:2018. Most entries are definitional with tolerance 0, because the constants of CIELAB are exact rationals chosen so the two branches of f meet exactly: kappa x epsilon is exactly 8, and (kappa x epsilon + 16)/116 is bit-identical to cbrt(epsilon). Writing them as decimals breaks that join and puts a step in the curve at the darkest end — which is the end this product lives at.

entries.source: CIE 15:2018, CIELAB — the actual CIE values, 216/24389
CIE 15:2018, CIELAB — the actual CIE values, 24389/27
CIE 15:2018 — the reference white has L* = 100 and no chromatic component, by construction
CIE 15:2018 — all ratios zero take the linear branch; f(0) = 16/116 for all three, so a* and b* vanish
CIE 15:2018 — at Y/Yn = epsilon the curve switches branches, and L* there is exactly kappa x epsilon = 8
CIE 15:2018, linear branch: L* = kappa x (Y/Yn) for Y/Yn <= epsilon
entries.derivationNote: Y/Yn = 0.004 <= epsilon, so L* = 903.2962962962963 x 0.004 = 3.6131851851851854. Tolerance is 2e-15 rather than 0 because the standard computes L* as 116 x f - 16 with f = (kappa x t + 16)/116, and 116 x ((x + 16)/116) - 16 is not bit-identical to x in float64 — the divide and the multiply each round. Following the standard's formulation is worth 1.3e-15; algebraically simplifying it to kappa x t would be an implementation that is no longer the published one.

entries.source: CIE 15:2018 with the sRGB transfer function (IEC 61966-2-1)
entries.derivationNote: sRGB 0.5 linearises to 0.21404114048223255, which is the Y ratio for a neutral. Y/Yn > epsilon, so L* = 116 x cbrt(0.21404114048223255) - 16 = 53.38896474111432. A neutral has a* = b* = 0 exactly, because all three ratios are equal and f is applied to each.

entries.source: CIE 15:2018 against the chromaticity-derived D65 white point; sRGB red primary from IEC 61966-2-1
entries.derivationNote: XYZ = [0.41239079926595934, 0.21263900587151027, 0.01933081871559182], white = [0.9504559270516716, 1, 1.0890577507598784]. NOTE: tables quoting Lab [53.2408, 80.0925, 67.2032] use the ROUNDED white point [0.95047, 1, 1.08883]; the two differ by 0.004 dE76 and the difference is entirely in the white point, not in the formula.

CIE 15:2018 — CIELCh is CIELAB in polar form; C* = hypot(a*, b*), h = atan2(b*, a*)
entries.derivationNote: From Lab [53.23711559542936, 80.09011352310385, 67.20326351172214]: C = hypot(80.0901, 67.2033) = 104.55001152926587, h = atan2(67.2033, 80.0901) in degrees = 39.99986515439815 — within 0.00014 degrees of 40, which is a fact about the sRGB primaries and not a rounding of ours.

From Lab [32.30087290398018, 79.1952703074042, -107.85546553974265]: b* is negative, so the raw atan2 is negative and folds to 306.28880325729324 degrees. An implementation that forgets to fold reports -53.7 and every hue comparison against it is wrong.
